questions.template: In the number {h}{t}{o}, what is the value of the {h}?
questions.hint: The {h} sits in the HUNDREDS column — three places from the right!
questions.explain: {h}{t}{o} is {h} hundreds, {t} tens and {o} ones — so the {h} is worth {h}00.

questions.hint: The tens digit is the one on the LEFT in a 2-digit number.
questions.explain: {t}{o} is made of {t} tens and {o} ones.

questions.hint: Only the TENS digit changes when you add 10.
questions.explain: {n} + 10 = {answer} — the tens digit went up by one.

questions.hint: Compare hundreds first, then tens, then ones!
questions.explain: {a} has the most when you check the columns left to right.

questions.template: In {th}{h}{t}{o}, what is the value of the digit {th}?
questions.hint: Four digits means the front one counts THOUSANDS.
questions.explain: {th}{h}{t}{o} = {th} thousands, {h} hundreds, {t} tens, {o} ones. The {th} is worth {th}000.

questions.hint: Look at the ONES digit — {u} is less than 5, so round DOWN.
questions.explain: {t}{u} is closer to {t}0 than to {t+1}0, because the ones digit {u} is under 5.

questions.hint: The ones digit is {u} — that's 5 or more, so round UP!
questions.explain: {t}{u} is closer to {t+1}0, because {u} is 5 or more.
{n} + 1,000 = {answer}. The thousands digit went up by one; everything else stayed.

questions.hint: Check the TENS digit: {t} is 5 or more, so round up to the next hundred.
questions.explain: {h}{t}{o} rounds to {answer} because the tens digit {t} pushes it up.

questions.hint: Build it column by column — thousands, hundreds, TENS (empty!), ones.
questions.explain: {th} thousands + {h} hundreds + {o} ones = {answer}. The tens column is a zero — don't lose it!

questions.template: Which number is closest to {a}000: {a}0{c}0, {a-1}999 or {a}{c}00?
questions.explain: {a-1}999 + 1 = {a}000, so it's just one step away — closer than the others.
